thread:
Mike H.: quick heads-up — ran the end-to-end perf sweep on canary today, attaching brief notes below. major regression observed when kv-miss rate > 12%: tail p99 token latency jumps ~2.8x and batch formation stalls.
Anya R.: ouch. is that the new kernel hint change we rolled last week?
Mike H.: looks correlated. kernel-selection now prefers small-seq kernels for throughput; when kv-miss causes longer sequences, we fall back and recompile path which stalls batcher.
Lee J.: can you paste the flamegraph snippet or perf counters?
Mike H.: pasted the snippet from the profiler:```
# perf snippet
BatchWaitLoop
  -> assemble_batches (60%)
  -> kernel_selector (20%)
  -> kv_fetch (15%)
  -> rpc_wait (5%)
```
Anya R.: so assemble_batches dominates during high miss. means queueing/formation logic is spinning waiting for prefetched tokens?
Mike H.: exactly. continuous-batcher waits up to max_batch_delay hoping to coalesce, but with variable seq lengths and kv-miss we get a lot of tiny microbatches then a big stall when a long request finally arrives.
Dave K.: practical mitigation ideas? immediate thought: tighten max_batch_delay for lanes with low KV locality, and add a token-budget per-lane to avoid starving kernel warmups.
Lee J.: +1. also consider a soft admission early-reject for requests that would blow active_token_budget. return a soft 429 with hint to retry-after small backoff.
Anya R.: we already have soft-429 path but it's global. need per-lane and kv-locality-aware. Could we compute a kv_hit_score for incoming request and route through a 'fastpath' admit check?
Mike H.: proposal: pre-admit checks in this order:
1) estimate_tokens(request) + active_tokens_in_batch_lane <= lane_token_target? else soft-429
2) if kv_hit_est < threshold then prefer small_seq_kernel and preemptive microbatch cap = 8 tokens
3) if kernel selector triggers fallback compile, mark lane in probation for 200ms and apply aggressive reject probability p=0.3
Implementation sketch:```
# pseudo
if (active_tokens + est_tokens > token_target) return soft429("retry-ms=40");
if (kv_hit_score < 0.7) set_batch_limit(8);
if (recent_kernel_fallbacks > 0) set_reject_prob(0.3);
```
Dave K.: sounds sensible. how do we pick token_target? static or adaptive?
Mike H.: adaptive preferred. start with lane_token_target = median_tokens_per_batch * 1.6, with clamps [32, 512]. adjust every 30s based on measured tail latency and kv-miss rate.
Lee J.: need guardrails so it doesn't oscillate. add hysteresis: only change if sustained shift >10% for two consecutive windows.
Anya R.: monitoring: add new metrics: lane_token_target, kv_hit_est, kernel_fallback_count, pre_admit_soft429_rate. dashboard tile and alert if soft429>1% sustained for 5m.
infra-bot: perf_canary_deploy #17588822 completed — canary nodes with kernel-hint-optimizer v2 rolled to 10% traffic.
Mike H.: thanks. next steps: I'll draft a small PR to add pre-admit check + per-lane token budget (will target a behind-flag rollout). want Lee and Anya to review the heuristics.
Lee J.: will review tomorrow. for the PR unit tests: simulate kv-hit 0%/50%/100% and assert that batch sizes and soft429 rates behave within expected bands.
Anya R.: add e2e perf job that flips kernel hint on/off and runs a 30m sustained mix to validate no p99 regression.
Dave K.: one more note — for tracing, emit span when we return soft-429 with the reason and current lane_token_target so downstream can introspect.
Mike H.: agreed. I'll include trace annotations. thanks all :thumbsup:
Anya R.: can we also add a quick playbook entry for oncall: if p99 spikes after deploy, set lane_token_target /= 1.5 and enable kernel-hint-fallback=false, then roll back.
Dave K.: adding playbook step: "if soft429 > 5% and p99 > threshold, flip flag and reduce targets; escalate if lasting >15m"
Mike H.: putting the follow-ups in a small GH issue and linking to this thread.
Anya R.: nice. short-term mitigation + better admission controls should prevent the microburst + stall pattern.
Mike H.: closing loop — PR by EOD tomorrow, canary run, then roll to 50% if stable.
